theme: 3 terms on errors in depth: passing an error up to the caller, naming the exact error type a function throws, and the return type of a function that never returns

terms.definition: Passing an error up to the caller with `try`, instead of catching it where it happens.
terms.example: Let Error Propagation do the work, and catch it once in the view model.

terms.definition: Writing the error type in parentheses after `throws`, so callers know exactly which error can come out.
terms.example: With Typed Throws, the `catch` block already knows it's a `SyncError`.

terms.definition: The return type `Never`, for a function that never returns, like `fatalError`, so it can end a `guard`.
terms.example: `stop` returns the Never Type, so the compiler knows the code after it can't run.

video.description:
Learn to explain errors in depth: Error Propagation, Typed Throws & Never Type, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Error Propagation - Passing an error up to the caller with `try`, instead of catching it where it happens.
Typed Throws - Writing the error type in parentheses after `throws`, so callers know exactly which error can come out.
Never Type - The return type `Never`, for a function that never returns, like `fatalError`, so it can end a `guard`.

Explain Error Propagation, Typed Throws & Never Type in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
에러 전파, 타입 지정 throws, Never 타입 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Error Propagation - Passing an error up to the caller with `try`, instead of catching it where it happens.
한국어: 에러 전파: 에러가 난 곳에서 잡지 않고 `try`로 호출한 쪽에 넘기는 것

Typed Throws - Writing the error type in parentheses after `throws`, so callers know exactly which error can come out.
한국어: 타입 지정 throws: `throws` 뒤 괄호에 에러 타입을 적어서, 호출하는 쪽이 어떤 에러가 나올지 정확히 알게 하는 것

Never Type - The return type `Never`, for a function that never returns, like `fatalError`, so it can end a `guard`.
한국어: Never 타입: `fatalError`처럼 절대 돌아오지 않는 함수의 반환 타입 `Never`로, `guard`를 끝낼 수 있음

dialogue.title: Where does the error go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `sync` has no catch. Where does the error go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Up to the caller. That's Error Propagation. `try` just passes it along.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So whoever calls `sync` has to handle it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Error Propagation stops at the first `do` and `catch`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And why does `throws` have `SyncError` in parentheses?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Typed Throws. The caller knows the exact error type.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `catch` gets a `SyncError`, not just any error?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. With Typed Throws, you can switch over the cases.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And `stop` returns `Never`? What does that mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's the Never Type. The function never returns, it just ends the app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. So I'd use the Never Type only for states that should be impossible.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's no catch here. Is that a bug?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, it's Error Propagation. The caller catches it.
